stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Allegations of Affair with Chinese Spy
stories.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia following reports of his involvement with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be linked to espionage activities. The resignation comes amid growing scrutiny from shareholders and lawmakers regarding his relationships, which have raised national security concerns. CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO.

stories.title: Israeli Airstrike on Gaza Hospital Claims Six Lives, Including a Doctor and a Child
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, resulted in the deaths of at least six individuals, including a doctor and a teenage boy. The attack, which occurred early on November 12, also left at least 27 others injured, according to health officials. This incident marks a significant escalation in violence amid an already fragile ceasefire in the region.

stories.title: Scott Colom Elected as Mississippi's First Black US Senator Since Reconstruction
stories.summary: Scott Colom, a Democrat, has been elected as Mississippi's first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction, defeating incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith in a closely contested race. Colom's victory, confirmed after a narrow margin of fewer than 5,000 votes, marks a significant political shift in the traditionally conservative state. This election also makes him the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Mississippi since 1982.

stories.title: Defense Secretary Hegseth Awards Medal to Soldier for Reprimanding Group at Tomb
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth awarded Specialist Thomas Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal after Iglesias reprimanded Hegseth and his group for making noise at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. The incident occurred following a Veterans Day ceremony, where the soldier insisted on maintaining silence and respect at the solemn memorial site.

stories.summary: A shooting at a gym in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle resulted in one death and four injuries. Police later confirmed that the suspect is dead, having apparently turned the gun on himself.
